halls.review: The companion names the sampler but omits the selected learner update binding. Canvas y maps to local Z before display rotation. Existing wrap lines and RESET/SPEED do not implement a controlled timestep comparison.

halls.focus: Reuse two world positions, predict their difference under a common shift and compare short, long and zero cases. Briefly explain normalization and its zero threshold; projections and readouts are supplied.

builds_on.why: Subtracting positions gives a displacement and scalar length.
World and display frames must be distinguished.

halls.adds: Practice of displacement with an explicit normalization return and threshold.
halls.carries: A direction-and-magnitude account that separates measured data from its scaled drawing.
halls.review: The companion lists normalization thresholds but does not explain division by length as the selected learner operation. Translation has not yet delivered its proposed normalization practice; supply or teach this short return explicitly.

halls.focus: Predict a+b, swap the contributions and compare two-leg distance with the direct route. Cancel with b=-a and account for the excluded reset; carriage movement and wall drawing are supplied.

builds_on.why: Displacement and length retain different information.
A running sum can accumulate neighbouring distances.
An ordered route preserves intermediate travel.

halls.adds: Deepens vector addition by separating summed destination from summed travelled lengths.
halls.carries: A result vector and route-distance account in a declared local frame.

halls.focus: Project the actual gap onto a supplied unit rail, subtract the kept vector and recombine. Predict the effect of rail reversal and perpendicular input movement; controls and diagrams are supplied.

builds_on.why: Subtraction gives the gap between positions.
A normalized axis supplies direction independently of length.
Vector sums can recombine contributions.

halls.adds: Adds signed scalar projection, its vector component and complementary remainder.
halls.carries: A projection-plus-remainder construction with an explicit receiving axis.

halls.focus: Evaluate the supplied position-at-time formula and vary one beginning. Compare complementary angles and distinguish a slower local clock from stronger gravity; conversion, duration and analytic marker display are supplied.

builds_on.why: Elapsed time is an input to a prescribed position.
Rate has declared units.
Vector components and display scale have separate meanings.

halls.adds: Adds velocity and acceleration units in a supplied analytic prediction; no integrator is introduced.
halls.carries: A position-at-time function with equal-height, uniform-gravity and no-drag assumptions.

halls.focus: Author a finite force pulse for the supplied rigid body and predict delta-v from force, mass and duration. Compare COAST with stopping the body, using drag-off runs before contact; integration and readouts are supplied.

builds_on.why: Initial velocity is distinct from a position evaluated at time.
Rate and accumulated change have stated units.
A timed condition can delimit a command.

halls.adds: Adds a force receiver whose velocity persists after the command ends.
halls.carries: A force schedule and quantitative velocity-change prediction.
halls.review: The existing operating/source companion explains the engine force command but does not provide the proposed learner schedule binding. Pass force in newtons without another dt factor; COAST alone leaves optional damping active.

halls.focus: Compare setting velocity from a field with adding acceleration to retained velocity, then update position. Predict two uniform steps before sink motion; field, unit adapters, runner and trails are supplied.

builds_on.why: A follower resamples at its current position.
Velocity can survive a changed command.
A finite update accumulates a rate over time.

halls.adds: Adds explicit position/velocity state and an assignment-versus-accumulation comparison.
halls.carries: A small update convention reusable by later forces, with its receiver units stated.
halls.review: The source rules are described, but the proposed reduced learner function and runner connection are absent. The markers have no mass or collisions and sample different values after their positions diverge; no learner state travels between halls.

halls.focus: Write one drag calculation F=-b*v and predict initial acceleration for two masses at equal speed. Keep the engine integration supplied; walking resistance, nominal mower work and circular motion remain separate comparisons.

builds_on.why: The engine integrates force commands for a body with mass.
Force, acceleration and assigned velocity require different receiving operations.

halls.adds: Adds a force that depends on the receiver's current velocity.
halls.carries: A reusable linear resistance calculation with coefficient units and receiver responsibility.
halls.review: The companion documents -b*v but does not bind a learner drag function. WALK uses a separate multiplier, mower work is nominal and the ring prescribes motion; none substitutes for the chosen force exercise.

halls.focus: Add restoration and drag in one dimension, then update velocity and position. Predict force direction and crossing from equal beginnings; rail, handle, timestep runner and damping-ratio adapter are supplied.

builds_on.why: The proposed explicit state update separates velocity from position.
Resistance depends on velocity.
Displacement can measure distance from a chosen centre.

halls.adds: Adds F=-kx-cv to an existing state-update pattern; equilibrium need not mean rest.
halls.carries: A spring-damper calculation distinct from a prescribed sine animation.
halls.review: The current model is explained but the common learner update/binding is still proposed. DAMP selects a ratio, so fixed-ratio changes of mass or stiffness also change the coefficient; release starts from rest.

halls.focus: Introduce period and phase at the rods, then halve the paired dials' rate difference and predict their gap after thirty seconds. Hold the gap with SAME RATE; displays and controls are supplied.

builds_on.why: An angle can advance with elapsed seconds.
A rate difference accumulates a change.
Returning motion motivates a cycle without already teaching phase.

halls.adds: Introduces period and phase; deepens assigned offsets versus accumulated rate difference.
halls.carries: A quantitative prediction of two stored angles under changed rates.

halls.focus: Apply paired interaction contributions to declared receivers and compare unequal masses before integration. Supply the softened attraction law and stepper; inspect the omitted response of a held source.

builds_on.why: Separation supplies an interaction's direction and length.
Force and receiving mass determine acceleration.
Independent bodies need separately retained state.

halls.adds: Adds distributing one interaction to two recipients rather than writing a new gravity solver.
halls.carries: A pairwise contribution pattern with explicit fixed or responsive recipients.
halls.review: The tutorial describes the model but does not teach the proposed two-contribution exercise. The fixed and mutual stations also change masses and initial states, so their paths cannot isolate source release alone.

halls.focus: Predict adjacent versus diagonal support for the same centred load, then release and compare. The hull and physics solver are supplied; contrast the commanded walker with the plate's contact response.

builds_on.why: A boundary can describe a geometric region.
Engine-integrated motion differs from prescribed placement.

halls.adds: Practice and physical comparison of geometry and mass; no new hull or gait implementation.
halls.carries: An explicit support hypothesis with assumptions about pads, load and contact.

halls.focus: Hold positions fixed, insert the screen and predict target eligibility before feeding begins. Compare selection with completed-meal history; selector, sight test and controller remain supplied.

builds_on.why: Distance can enter a condition.
A current test differs from retained state.
Commanded behaviour and physical validation are different kinds of evidence.

halls.adds: Reflective practice of conditions and retained events; no new controller syntax.
halls.carries: A distinction between eligible targets, recorded events and attributed agency.

halls.focus: Use the cubes to predict zero acceleration versus an immediate stop, then compare the visitor's separate receiver. Compose existing controls; membership tests, damping and contact handling are supplied.

builds_on.why: Acceleration changes stored velocity rather than replacing it.
A body retains motion when a command ends.
The field and recipient need named coordinate frames.

halls.adds: Composition of field input with declared receivers and entry/exit rules.
halls.carries: A receiver-aware account of acceleration, membership and persistent motion.

halls.focus: Predict the next search address from the cost gradient, step the supplied optimiser and compare starts, rates and thresholds. Surface, controls and trails are supplied; distinguish search iterations from physical time.

builds_on.why: Finite differences estimate local rates.
An update's state and units determine its meaning.
Retained velocity provides a contrast with this velocity-free search.

halls.adds: Adds a two-axis cost gradient and descent update with separate slope, frame and budget stops.
halls.carries: A local search rule with a declared objective, step and reason for stopping.

halls.focus: Compare the hand-shaped spline, formula washing lines and fixed surface. Change one span or sag input and state which constraints it retains; samplers, tubes and analytic examples are supplied.

builds_on.why: A profile or path can be evaluated by a supplied construction.
A function's inputs determine generated positions.
A computed objective must be distinguished from a drawn result.

halls.adds: Reflective comparison of drawn, evaluated and physically settled constructions; no required new syntax.
halls.carries: A curve specification that names its inputs and absent physical tests.
halls.review: Current prose calls the drafted sag curve gravity-derived and the fixed catenoid an instantly solved minimum. Align it with the actual spline/formula/static-surface comparison; decide whether a bounded code exercise is needed.

halls.focus: Use a short chain to correct neighbouring distances, guard zero separation and account for pinned endpoints. Compare correction counts with disturbance disabled; runner, line renderer and optional wind are supplied.

builds_on.why: Position history can be retained in ordered lists.
Neighbour distance gives a measurable error.
Connections are data separate from positions.

halls.adds: Adds repeated local distance correction under a finite computation budget.
halls.carries: A constrained network with explicit anchors, rest lengths and correction count.
halls.review: The current tutorial jumps through full cloth and frozen forms, divides by cur without a zero guard and overstates a one-over-passes law. The proposed short-chain binding and pinned-end correction explanation are absent.

halls.focus: Calculate two arm lengths across a chosen span and check equal mass-distance products. Supply modelled disc masses and geometry; inspect the heavier side nearer its pivot without claiming dynamic stability.

builds_on.why: Distances can become inputs to a numerical constraint.
A small returning function can generate geometry parameters.
Static balance is conditional and differs from a demonstrated dynamic response.

halls.adds: Adds an algebraic balance function; recursion and larger structural construction remain supplied.
halls.carries: A lever calculation with omitted rod/wire mass and other assumptions stated.
halls.review: The lever calculation is present, but the tutorial expands into untaught recursion and claims strength and force balance from prescribed geometry/scale motion. Select the small function and separate display from mechanical validation.

halls.focus: Propose bounded candidates, keep improvements and compare a zero-to-one draw with a supplied uphill probability. Separate current from best-so-far state and compare cooling; landscapes and controls are supplied.

builds_on.why: A cost function evaluates a proposed search address.
A condition selects which value to retain.
Current state and remembered state can serve different purposes.

halls.adds: Introduces a local bounded random draw and probability comparison before Randomness, then non-greedy search.
halls.carries: A probabilistic acceptance rule with separate current and best records.
halls.review: The tutorial uses randf/randf_range before explaining range and draw timing, and lacks the selected best-so-far exercise. Stagnation is not proof of entrapment and cooling does not guarantee escape or optimality.

halls.focus: Write height and low-movement-duration requirements for a supplied stack measurement, then test a still but rejected construction. Compare this predicate with optimiser restarts and the clock-driven forge; contacts and measurements are supplied.

builds_on.why: A current condition can update remembered state.
Elapsed time can accumulate while a condition holds.
A search stop does not itself establish a satisfactory outcome.

halls.adds: Composition of conditions, timers and criteria; no new syntax or universal optimum is introduced.
halls.carries: An explicit success criterion and a counterexample it correctly rejects.
halls.review: The tutorial omits the stack's height requirement and presents the clock-driven target/jitter as optimised physical form. Confirm the measurement interface and distinguish stability detection, search restarts and prescribed MAX Q appearance.
